text: Occupation: Mother/Business Owner
My name is Liz Peterson, and I'm running for the Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified School District Board because our schools shaped my family, and I want to protect what makes them work.

Both of my children went through PVPUSD; my youngest graduated this past year. I've spent those years volunteering rather than watching from the sidelines, serving in several PTA board positions and on the district's Local Control and Accountability committee from 2023 to 2025, where I helped review how the district sets priorities and spends its money.
That experience taught me the difference between a budget on paper and a classroom that has what it needs.

Our district faces real challenges. Declining enrollment is reshaping our schools and forcing hard decisions about facilities and staffing. And voters recently approved a bond that many residents opposed, which makes it more important that every dollar is spent transparently, on schedule, and on the projects promised.
I will push for honest budgeting, open communication with parents, and spending decisions this community can verify.
I'm not a politician. I'm a parent who stayed involved after graduation, because these schools belong to all of us.

text: My wife and I moved to Palos Verdes ten years ago for the outstanding schools. As a lifelong educator, including faculty at master's-level Test Pilot School and flight instructor, I'm running for School Board to maintain and strengthen the quality education our community expects and deserves.

To ensure my focus remains solely on our students, I created the Palos Verdes Peninsula Pledge: "I will not accept financial contributions from politicians, political parties, partisan PACs, or political organizations (including unions). If elected, I will serve my full term and will not run for any other office while on the Board." I invite all candidates to join this pledge and put students first.
My priorities are clear: high academic standards, safe and respectful campuses, fiscal responsibility paired with strong teacher support, and full parental transparency and involvement.

Our district receives $4,500 less per student than the state average — nearly $45 million each year. We need Board members who will actively advocate at the state level for fair funding so our students and teachers are not shortchanged.
I'm committed to practical governance that puts students first and to securing the funding needed to attract and retain the outstanding teachers our students deserve.

text: Age: 49
Occupation: CEO of Healthcare Company

Our schools are why families choose Palos Verdes - keeping them excellent takes more than good intentions. As budgets tighten across California, it takes board members with real CEO experience running complex budgets, who want every student in every school getting the same great education, and who treat the role as service, not politics.

I've spent my career being accountable for results and serving. As CEO of a healthcare company, matching complex budgets to the people they serve is my daily job. As a Naval Academy graduate, I served as a carrier-based Navy pilot in wartime, and hold an MBA from Harvard Business School.

More importantly, my wife and I chose this community for its schools and have been PVPUSD parents for over a decade. Our son attends high school here; I know firsthand what our schools do well and where they must do better.

On the board, I will protect academic rigor, keep every student safe and welcome, execute transparent budgets, support our teachers, and keep politics out of our classrooms. Whether or not your children fill them today, great public schools are the promise Palos Verdes keeps to every child. I would be honored to earn your vote.
